title: Many-Body Mobility Edge and Non-Hermitian Skin Effect in an Interacting Quasi-Periodic Spin Chain
authors: Lavoisier Wah, Ayan Banerjee, Flore K. Kunst
abstract: Non-Hermitian many-body physics reveals a rich interplay between topology, localization, and boundary effects, yet their collective behavior in interacting disordered systems remains largely unexplored. In this work, we study an interacting non-Hermitian spin chain subject to a quasi-periodic longitudinal field, providing a unified and controlled setting, where non-Hermitian dynamics, interactions, and localization mechanisms intertwine. Remarkably, we discover a "D-shaped" many-body mobility edge that separates extended and localized eigenstates, while simultaneously delineating regimes of many-body localization and the many-body skin effect (where many-body eigenstates acquire an anomalous drift towards a boundary under open boundaries) emerging from the combined action of interactions, non-Hermiticity, and driving amplitude. We demonstrate that the skin effect induces multifractal scaling in the non-Hermitian eigenstates, providing a clear signature of the many-body skin effect. Employing diagnostics such as the fractal dimension, complex eigenvalue fractions, and many-body inverse participation ratios, we map out a unified phase diagram in which all measures consistently identify the "D-shaped" mobility edge. Finally, we probe this interplay using both complex level-spacing statistics and dynamical observables such as density imbalance, entanglement growth, and wave-packet evolution, culminating in a rich many-body mobility phase diagram that captures both the many-body skin effect and localization transitions. Our results identify a clear, defining signature of the "D-shaped" many-body mobility edge, and underscore its pivotal role in shaping the physics of open quantum many-body systems.
summary: This paper explores how interactions, quasi-periodicity, and non-Hermitian physics combine to govern transport in spin chains. The key finding is the identification of a unique "D-shaped" mobility edge that separates different quantum phases. It provides a comprehensive phase diagram capturing both many-body localization and boundary-induced skin effects.
main_problem: The study investigates the complex interplay between non-Hermiticity, interactions, quasi-periodicity, and localization mechanisms in many-body quantum spin chains.
main_result: The authors discover a characteristic "D-shaped" many-body mobility edge that governs transitions between extended, localized (MBL), and skin effect regimes. They also confirm the signature of the many-body skin effect via multifractal scaling.
method: The research employs advanced numerical diagnostics such as fractal dimension ($D_q$), complex eigenvalue fractions, and analyzing finite-size flow directions of spectral measures.
model_or_system: The model is an interacting non-Hermitian spin chain subjected to a quasi-periodic longitudinal field. The Hamiltonian incorporates hopping terms, nearest-neighbor Ising interactions ($J$), and the disorder/quasi-periodicity ($h_i$).
key_observables: Many-body mobility edge (MBME), many-body skin effect (MBSE) signature, fractal dimension ($\langle D_q angle$), complex eigenvalue fractions, density imbalance, and entanglement growth.
important_parameters: Non-Hermitian asymmetry parameter ($\gamma$), interaction strength ($J$), quasi-periodic field amplitude ($h$), and the irrationality parameter $\alpha$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on mapping out a unified phase diagram by varying disorder strength ($h$) while keeping other parameters fixed or within specific regimes.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the energy spectrum in the complex plane for different disorder strengths and plots the energy-resolved multifractal dimension $D_2$ to map the mobility edge structure.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the spectral properties (PBC vs. OBC) using diagnostics like fractal dimensions, mapping out a unified phase diagram that captures transitions between MBL and MBSE regimes as disorder strength is varied.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the intersection of non-Hermiticity and localization in interacting systems, which is highly relevant for understanding open quantum systems where boundary effects (like skin effect) compete with intrinsic disorder-induced localization.
